pharm: Antihypertensive; selective angiotensin II type-1 (AT1) receptor antagonist
quick: 20 mg OD; may increase to 40 mg after 2 weeks
Decide to stop drug or nursing; no human data
summary: Olmesartan medoxomil is a prodrug ARB rapidly bioactivated to olmesartan, used to lower blood pressure in adults and children 6 years and older. It is dosed once daily, starting at 20 mg in adults and titrated to 40 mg after 2 weeks if needed. It carries a boxed warning for fetal toxicity and has been associated with a sprue-like enteropathy causing severe chronic diarrhea and weight loss.
indications: Treatment of hypertension in adults to lower blood pressure
Treatment of hypertension in pediatric patients 6 years of age and older
May be used alone or in combination with other antihypertensive agents

dosage.d: Start 20 mg once daily as monotherapy; may increase to 40 mg once daily
dosage.t: Titrate after 2 weeks if further BP reduction needed
dosage.n: Doses above 40 mg show no greater effect; twice-daily offers no advantage

dosage.d: Start 10 mg once daily; maximum 20 mg once daily
dosage.n: Weight-based; use extemporaneous 2 mg/mL suspension if unable to swallow tablets

dosage.d: Start 20 mg once daily; maximum 40 mg once daily

dosage.n: Correct volume/salt depletion or monitor closely (e.g. diuretic-treated)

admin: Take once daily, with or without food
Dosage must be individualized; titrate after 2 weeks if BP target not reached
For children unable to swallow tablets, use an extemporaneous 2 mg/mL suspension (refrigerate 2-8 C, use within 4 weeks; shake well before each use)
Initiate under close supervision and consider a lower start in volume- or salt-depleted patients
Not recommended in children <1 year of age
moa: Selectively blocks the binding of angiotensin II to the AT1 receptor in vascular smooth muscle, antagonizing angiotensin II-mediated vasoconstriction and aldosterone release independent of its synthesis pathway. Olmesartan has more than 12,500-fold greater affinity for the AT1 than AT2 receptor. Unlike ACE inhibitors it does not inhibit ACE (kininase II) and so does not affect bradykinin, resulting in less cough.

absolute: Co-administration of aliskiren in patients with diabetes
relative: Bilateral or unilateral renal artery stenosis
monitor: Dual RAS blockade with ACE inhibitors or aliskiren
Concurrent potassium-sparing diuretics, supplements, or potassium-containing salt substitutes
Pre-existing renal impairment or heart failure

preg: Boxed warning: when pregnancy is detected, discontinue as soon as possible. Drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system can cause fetal harm and death, especially in the second and third trimesters, reducing fetal renal function and causing oligohydramnios, lung hypoplasia, skull hypoplasia, anuria, hypotension, renal failure, and death. Consider alternative antihypertensive therapy; perform serial ultrasounds and monitor exposed neonates for hypotension, oliguria, and hyperkalemia.
lact: There is no information on the presence of olmesartan in human milk or its effects on the infant; it is secreted at low concentration in milk of lactating rats. Because of the potential for adverse effects, decide whether to discontinue nursing or the drug, considering its importance to the mother.
renal: Serum concentrations are elevated in renal insufficiency; AUC is approximately tripled in severe renal impairment (CrCl <20 mL/min). No initial dosage adjustment is recommended for moderate to marked renal impairment (CrCl <40 mL/min). Monitor renal function; pharmacokinetics in hemodialysis have not been studied.
hepatic: AUC is increased about 60% in moderate hepatic impairment. No initial dosage adjustment is recommended for patients with moderate to marked hepatic dysfunction.

major: Aliskiren in patients with diabetes - contraindicated
ACE inhibitors or aliskiren (dual RAS blockade) - increased hypotension, hyperkalemia, and renal impairment; generally avoid
Potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, or potassium-containing salt substitutes - hyperkalemia
moderate: NSAIDs including COX-2 inhibitors - reduced antihypertensive effect and risk of renal deterioration (especially elderly, volume-depleted, or renally impaired)
Lithium - increased serum lithium levels and toxicity; monitor levels
Colesevelam - reduces olmesartan exposure; give olmesartan at least 4 hours before colesevelam
minor: Digoxin and warfarin - no significant interaction reported
Antacids - no significant effect on bioavailability
interactions.food: Food does not affect bioavailability; may be given with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: May potentiate the hypotensive effect; advise caution.
interactions.diagnostics: May increase serum potassium, creatinine, and BUN.

serious: Symptomatic hypotension in volume- or salt-depleted patients
Acute renal failure / worsening renal function
Sprue-like enteropathy (severe chronic diarrhea with substantial weight loss, villous atrophy)

monitoring: Blood pressure at baseline and follow-up
Serum potassium, particularly with diuretics, renal insufficiency, or diabetes
Renal function (creatinine, BUN) after initiation and dose changes
Watch for severe chronic diarrhea and weight loss (sprue-like enteropathy)
counsel: Take once daily, with or without food, at the same time each day
Stop the drug and contact your provider immediately if you become pregnant
Rise slowly to reduce dizziness; report fainting
Avoid potassium supplements and salt substitutes unless advised
Report severe, persistent diarrhea or unexplained weight loss (may require switching therapy)
Report swelling of the face, lips, or throat (angioedema)
pk: Peak antihypertensive effect within about 2 weeks; steady state in 3-5 days
pearls: Prodrug rapidly and completely bioactivated by ester hydrolysis to olmesartan during absorption
Not metabolized by CYP450; clinically significant drug-metabolism interactions are not expected
Sprue-like enteropathy may appear months to years after starting; exclude other causes and consider alternative therapy
High-dose olmesartan (40 mg/day) may raise CV risk in diabetics per the ROADMAP trial, though data are not conclusive
Less cough and angioedema than ACE inhibitors; avoid dual RAS blockade
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip it and resume the usual once-daily schedule; do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Limited human data. The most likely manifestations are hypotension and tachycardia; bradycardia may occur if vagal stimulation occurs. Treat symptomatic hypotension with supportive care, supine positioning, and IV normal saline. The dialyzability of olmesartan is unknown.
